test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 22 Jan 2021 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Name the Governor-General under whom a new policy of ‘paramountcy’ was initiated.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Hasting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Hastings** instituted the policy of paramountcy. From 1813 until 1823, he served as** Governor-General of India**.
 
• The corporation became the supreme law, the supreme power, and to defend its interests, it justified the conquest of any Indian country under this policy.
 
• When the British attempted to conquer the minor states of Karnataka during this process, Rani Channamma led an anti-British resistance movement.
 
• **Lord Hastings or Lord Moira** was Governor-General of India for ten years, from 1813 to 1823.
 
• His administration is remembered for its interventionist and war policies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **On April 22, 1812, Lord Dalhousie**, Governor-General of India from 1848 to 1856, was born. He instituted the** Doctrine of Lapse **policy, which was one of the key causes of the 1857 Revolt.
 
• **From 1798 to 1805, Lord Wellesley **served as Governor-General of Fort Williams. During his reign, the Fourth and final Anglo-Mysore war was fought, in which Tipu was killed.
 
• **Charles Cornwallis,** 1st Marquess Cornwallis was appointed Governor-General of Fort William (Bengal) and Commander-in-Chief of British India on September 12, 1786.
